items.title: Read the settings that keep a new bucket private
items.kills: "A new bucket is public and unencrypted until you change its settings."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Keep your account ID in the variable ACCOUNT_ID for the next step.
steps.expect: No output. The variable ACCOUNT_ID now holds your account ID.

steps.text: Read the Block Public Access settings of the whole account. S3 combines them with the settings of each bucket and applies the most restrictive combination.
steps.expect: Either the four settings BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets with true or false, or an error. An error that no configuration was found means the account has no account-level setting.

steps.text: List the names of your buckets. If the list is empty, stop here: the last two steps need a bucket.
steps.expect: A list of bucket names, or an empty list.

steps.text: Pick one bucket from the list as <BUCKET>. Read the Block Public Access settings of that bucket.
steps.expect: The same four settings, each true for a bucket that kept its defaults. An error that no configuration was found means the bucket has no setting of its own; the account settings of step 2 still apply.

steps.text: Read the default encryption of the same bucket.
steps.expect: ["AES256"], the name of SSE-S3, for a bucket that kept its defaults. A bucket that uses SSE-KMS shows aws:kms instead. No bucket shows an empty result.

items.title: Share a private object with a presigned URL that expires
items.kills: "A browser can download from a private bucket only if the bucket is made public."
items.cost: about $0: one object of a few kilobytes for some minutes and a few requests; S3 has no minimum charge
items.cost_if_forgotten: about $0 a day: one object of a few kilobytes
items.read_only_alternative: This alternative creates no resource. Choose an object that you can already read in a bucket of your account as <BUCKET> and <KEY>. Run aws s3 presign s3://<BUCKET>/<KEY> --expires-in 60, open the URL in a browser tab, wait 2 minutes and reload the tab. The first load shows the object; the second shows AccessDenied.

steps.text: Choose 8 random lowercase letters and digits as <SUFFIX>: bucket names are global, so a plain name is often taken. Create the bucket in the Region of your CloudShell session.
steps.expect: make_bucket: saa-s3-t02- and your suffix. If the name is taken, choose another suffix and use it in every later command.

steps.text: Tag the bucket with the book tag and the task tag.
steps.expect: No output.

steps.text: Upload the small text file /etc/os-release as the object note.txt. Linux systems keep their name and version in this file.
steps.command: aws s3api put-object --bucket saa-s3-t02-<SUFFIX> --key note.txt --body /etc/os-release --content-type text/plain
steps.expect: JSON with an ETag and "ServerSideEncryption": "AES256". You asked for no encryption, and the object is encrypted with SSE-S3.

steps.text: Read the object without a signature, as a stranger on the internet would. <REGION> is the Region code of your CloudShell session, for example us-east-1.
steps.expect: An XML error with the code AccessDenied. The bucket is private.

steps.text: Create a presigned URL for note.txt that expires in 60 seconds. The command signs the URL with the credentials of your CloudShell session.
steps.expect: One long https URL. Its query string holds X-Amz-Expires=60, X-Amz-Credential and X-Amz-Signature.

steps.text: Copy the URL and open it in a new browser tab within the minute.
steps.expect: The text of the file, with lines such as NAME and VERSION. The bucket is still private.

steps.text: Wait until 2 minutes have passed since you created the URL. Reload the same browser tab.
steps.expect: An XML error with the code AccessDenied and a message that the request has expired.
steps.predict: The URL, the object and the bucket have not changed. What does the tab show now?
steps.explain: S3 checks the expiry [at the time of the HTTP request](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-reusable-until-expiry), so the same URL now fails. The URL is [limited by the permissions of the user](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-creator-needs-permission) who created it, and it lends that permission for a limited time. When the signer used temporary credentials, [the URL expires when the credential expires](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-expires-with-temporary-credentials), even before its own expiry time.

steps.text: Fix it: create a new presigned URL that expires in 300 seconds, and open the new URL in the tab.
steps.expect: A new URL. The tab shows the text again until this URL expires.

verify.expect: An error that shows 404 (Not Found): the bucket no longer exists.

still_costs: Nothing you would notice: the storage charge depends on the size of the objects and on how long they are stored, and note.txt is a few kilobytes. Delete the bucket anyway, so that no unused bucket stays in the account.

items.title: Delete a versioned object and get it back
items.kills: "In a versioned bucket a delete removes the object, and a delete can never destroy data for good."
items.cost: about $0: two versions of a few kilobytes for some minutes and a few requests; S3 has no minimum charge
items.cost_if_forgotten: about $0 a day: a few kilobytes, but every version stays billed until you delete it by its version ID
items.read_only_alternative: This alternative creates nothing. If a bucket in your account has versioning turned on, use it as <BUCKET> and run aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket <BUCKET> --max-items 20. Each entry under DeleteMarkers with IsLatest true is a deleted object whose older versions are still stored.

steps.text: Choose 8 random lowercase letters and digits as <SUFFIX>. Create the bucket in the Region of your CloudShell session.
steps.expect: make_bucket: saa-s3-t03- and your suffix. If the name is taken, choose another suffix and use it in every later command.

steps.text: Tag the bucket with the book tag and the task tag.
steps.expect: No output.

steps.text: Turn on versioning. A new bucket starts with versioning off.
steps.expect: No output.

steps.text: Upload the small text file /etc/os-release as note.txt. Keep the version ID of this first version in V1.
steps.command: aws s3api put-object --bucket saa-s3-t03-<SUFFIX> --key note.txt --body /etc/os-release --content-type text/plain
steps.expect: No output. V1 now holds a long version ID.

steps.text: Delete note.txt the usual way, with no version ID. Keep the version ID that the delete returns in MARKER.
steps.expect: No output. MARKER now holds a second, new version ID.

steps.text: Read note.txt with a plain request that names no version ID. The command asks for the metadata of the object.
steps.expect: An error with 404 and Not Found.
steps.predict: You deleted note.txt, but versioning is on. Does the read work, and is the data gone?
steps.explain: Your delete named no version ID, so S3 added a delete marker, which [becomes the current (or newest) version](../facts/s3.md#s3-delete-marker-soft-delete). A plain GET of note.txt now returns [404 Not Found](../facts/s3.md#s3-versioning-get-delete-marker-404), and this plain HEAD request gets the same answer. The first version is still stored, and it [can be retrieved or restored](../facts/s3.md#s3-versioning-preserves-on-overwrite-and-delete).

steps.text: Fix it: copy the first version onto the same key, with the task tags. The copy becomes the current version of note.txt. Keep its version ID in V2.
steps.command: aws s3api copy-object --bucket saa-s3-t03-<SUFFIX> --key note.txt --copy-source "saa-s3-t03-<SUFFIX>/note.txt?versionId=$V1" --tagging-directive REPLACE --tagging "book=saa&task=s3-t03"
steps.expect: No output. V2 now holds the version ID of the restored copy.

steps.text: List every version and every delete marker of note.txt. Find the entry that is the latest.
steps.command: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket saa-s3-t03-<SUFFIX> --prefix note.txt --query "{versions: Versions[].[VersionId,IsLatest], markers: DeleteMarkers[].[VersionId,IsLatest]}"
steps.expect: Two versions and one delete marker. The copy (V2) shows true; the first version and the marker show false. Nothing was lost.

cleanup.text: Delete the restored copy by its version ID. A delete that names a version ID removes that version permanently. If CloudShell restarted, step 8 shows the IDs again.
Delete the delete marker by its version ID.
Delete the first version by its version ID. The bucket is now empty.

verify.expect: An error that shows 404 (Not Found): the bucket no longer exists.

still_costs: Every version left in a versioned bucket is billed as storage, because S3 charges for each version of an object. If delete-bucket fails, run step 8 again and delete each entry it lists by its version ID.
